gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a Denon DCD-600NE left powered but idle draws 12 W against 0.3 W in standby, that its 30-minute Auto Standby ships switched off, or that the Yamaha-vs-Denon running-cost gap works out to about 1.5 kWh a year at 2 h of play a day.
standout_why: Inside Out Home Reviews (read 2026-11-08) gives prices, weights, dimensions, DAC bit depth and warranty but explicitly no power consumption, output voltage or S/N, so it cannot derive running cost or gain matching. The Yamaha USA spec page, both Crutchfield compares, the Crutchfield CD-S303 product page, B&H compare and Sweetwater page all returned 403 to my fetches, so I could not confirm what they state; Crutchfield compares normally list weight and outputs but not power draw. The Onkyo support article only gives the optical output format. The derived kWh-per-year, idle-vs-standby ratio and output-level match are new, but they show the two players are practically identical on these numbers, so they do not by themselves decide the pick.
decides: Running cost cannot separate the Yamaha CD-S303 and Denon DCD-600NE: 11 W vs 12 W playing and 0.2 W vs 0.3 W in standby is about 1.5 kWh a year apart at 2 h/day. What does matter is behaviour: the Denon ships with Auto Standby off, so a forgotten unit burns 12 W around the clock (about 105 kWh/yr) until the owner holds POWER 5 s to enable the 30-minute timer. Both put out 2.0 V RMS on RCA, so neither needs a different amp input gain; the FiiO DM13 line out is 2.5 V RMS, about 1.9 dB hotter, which matters if the shopper is weighing the portable FiiO against a full-width deck for the same stereo.
